cards.question: What kind of drive is an EBS volume?
cards.answer: A network drive (not a physical drive)

cards.question: What common analogy describes an EBS volume?
How does an EBS volume communicate with an EC2 instance, and what does that imply for performance?
cards.answer: Over the network; there may be a bit of latency

cards.question: Which storage choice lets an instance persist data even after the instance is terminated: instance store or EBS?
Can an EBS volume be detached from one instance and attached to another quickly?
cards.answer: Yes, it can be re-attached quickly

cards.question: What is an EBS volume bound to?
Can a volume in us-east-1a be attached to an instance in us-east-1b?
cards.answer: No — the volume is locked to its AZ

cards.question: An instance in us-east-1b needs an existing us-east-1a volume. What must you do?
cards.answer: Snapshot the volume, then restore it in us-east-1b

cards.question: At the CCP level, how many instances can an EBS volume be mounted to at a time?
An instance in us-east-1a needs the volume while an instance in us-east-1b keeps it mounted. Is that possible?
cards.answer: No — one instance at a time, and the volume stays in one AZ

cards.question: What two capacity dimensions does an EBS volume have provisioned up front?
How is EBS billing calculated relative to usage?
cards.answer: You are billed for all the provisioned capacity

cards.question: A 100 GB volume is only 10% full. How much capacity are you billed for?
Does an unattached EBS volume avoid provisioned-capacity billing?
cards.answer: No — an unattached volume still incurs provisioned-capacity billing

cards.question: Can an EBS volume's capacity be changed after creation?
cards.answer: Yes, you can increase capacity over time

cards.question: What is an EBS snapshot?
cards.answer: A point-in-time backup of an EBS volume
cards.keyTopic: Snapshot to move volume across AZ

cards.question: Is detaching a volume required before taking a snapshot?
cards.keyTopic: Snapshot to move volume across AZ

cards.question: What is the standard way to move a volume across Availability Zones?
cards.answer: Snapshot it, then restore the snapshot in the target AZ
cards.keyTopic: Snapshot to move volume across AZ

cards.question: Besides AZs, what else can EBS snapshots be copied across?
cards.keyTopic: Snapshot to move volume across AZ

cards.question: A volume must be moved across AZs. Which is used: detach and attach, or snapshot and restore?
cards.keyTopic: Snapshot to move volume across AZ

cards.question: What does the Delete on Termination attribute control?
cards.answer: Whether the EBS volume is deleted when the attached instance terminates

cards.question: Through which interfaces can Delete on Termination be controlled?
What is the main use case for disabling Delete on Termination on the root volume?
cards.answer: Preserve the root volume when the instance is terminated

cards.question: By default, what happens to the root EBS volume when an EC2 instance terminates?
By default, what happens to non-root attached EBS volumes when the instance terminates?
Which volumes are deleted by default at termination: root only, or all attached volumes?

groups.concept: Snapshot features: Archive, Recycle Bin, FSR

cards.question: How much cheaper is EBS Snapshot Archive than standard snapshots?
How long does restoring a snapshot from EBS Snapshot Archive take?
Rarely restored backups need minimum cost and slow restore is acceptable. Which feature?
A workload needs fast restore. Is Archive the right choice?
cards.answer: No — archive restore takes 24 to 72 hours

cards.question: What is the Recycle Bin for EBS Snapshots used for?
cards.answer: Retain deleted snapshots so they can be recovered after accidental deletion

cards.question: What retention range can you specify in Recycle Bin for EBS Snapshots?
A snapshot was deleted by mistake. Which feature allows recovery?
Which feature answers "first read from a restored volume is too slow": Recycle Bin or FSR?
What does Fast Snapshot Restore do to the snapshot?
cards.answer: Forces full initialization so there is no latency on first use

cards.question: How does Fast Snapshot Restore affect cost?
Which feature reduces snapshot cost: Fast Snapshot Restore or EBS Snapshot Archive?
On the SAA exam, is EBS multi-attach a way to use a volume from a different AZ?
